# Pillow

Python's imaging library. Used in lab 11 of [[python-programming-laboratories]] for cover-image
processing inside a four-stage document pipeline — fetch, extract, render, assemble — that turns a
scraped book into a `.docx` with generated charts.

## The version break it documents

> "**Two library APIs moved.** `Image.ANTIALIAS` and `ImageDraw.textsize` were removed in Pillow 10;
> `findAll(text=True)` was removed in BeautifulSoup 4.13."
> — Python-Programming-Laboratories/labs/11_report_pipeline/README.md, 2026-07-25

Both removals were long-deprecated aliases that a great deal of tutorial code still uses:

- `Image.ANTIALIAS` → `Image.Resampling.LANCZOS`. The constant was an alias, not a distinct filter,
  so the port is a rename with no behaviour change.
- `ImageDraw.textsize` → `textbbox` / `textlength`. This one *is* a behaviour change: `textbbox`
  returns a bounding box with offsets rather than a bare `(w, h)`, so any layout arithmetic built on
  the old return value needs adjusting rather than renaming.

Writing the diagnosis beside the code is the point — the commit history has none of this, since
everything landed in one day: [[import-finished-work-into-git]]. The pattern is
[[document-the-failure-mode-next-to-the-fix]]; the [[beautifulsoup]] half of the same note is
recorded there.

## Also handled: fonts off Windows

The pipeline includes a **font fallback** for non-Windows machines, because `ImageFont.truetype` on a
hard-coded Windows font path fails outright rather than substituting. Same class of problem as
`48ba16d Fix UnicodeEncodeError in the lab3 demos on Windows consoles` in
[[discrete-mathematics-laboratories]], from the opposite direction — one repo's code broke *on*
Windows, this one's would break *off* it.

Charts in the same pipeline come from [[matplotlib]] with `Agg` and a `plt.close()` per figure across
41 chapters; every generated artefact is gitignored as reproducible from source.
